stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a ‘doom loop’ for the web
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Court documents reveal OpenAI and Microsoft were warned about creating a 'doom loop' for the web.
The companies' internal documentation characterized their data scraping for model training as the 'largest theft of labor in human history.'
The story highlights significant legal and ethical concerns regarding large-scale AI data ingestion and copyright/labor rights.

stories.title: Security researchers used Claude to help them hack into OpenAI
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Security researchers leveraged Anthropic's Claude Opus models to compromise OpenAI employee accounts.
The breach reportedly allowed access to OpenAI's 'Monorepo' GitHub repository, containing proprietary algorithmic secrets.
The attack was executed rapidly, taking less than 72 hours to achieve access.

stories.title: AI hallucination of Chinese nuclear components almost led to US military attack
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI hallucination of Chinese nuclear components nearly triggered a US military response.
The incident highlights critical risks associated with deploying AI in sensitive military applications.
The overall trend indicates an accelerating integration of AI within military operations.

stories.title: FAA tees up $875M AI tool to help manage air traffic congestion
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is developing a substantial $875 million AI tool.
The primary purpose of the tool is to alleviate air traffic congestion.
Initial deployment will focus on managing air traffic in the Washington D.C. area before a broader rollout.

stories.title: Researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI
stories.author: Cristina Criddle, Financial Times
bullet_points: Researchers successfully leveraged Claude AI to compromise an OpenAI employee account.
The attack resulted in the exfiltration of sensitive data stored on GitHub belonging to OpenAI.
This incident highlights significant security vulnerabilities in large language models (LLMs) when used in adversarial contexts.

stories.title: Small AI models let drones autonomously identify and attack battlefield targets
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Small AI models are being deployed on drones for autonomous battlefield target identification and attack.
The technology utilizes decentralized, AI-driven learning systems.
The deployment is being implemented across military bases by Scaleout.

stories.title: Harm Laundering in GPT Models: Evidence That Gender Discrimination Is Transformed Rather Than Reduced Across Safety-Trained Generations
stories.author: Noura Al Moubayed
bullet_points: The study introduces the concept of 'harm laundering,' where explicit bias in LLMs is transformed rather than eliminated during safety training.
Researchers analyzed 450,000 gender-directed completions across GPT-2 through GPT-5 to demonstrate this systematic flaw in current safety evaluations.
The findings suggest that current surface-form classifiers used for safety testing are fundamentally incomplete in measuring true bias reduction.

stories.title: Harm Laundering in GPT Models: Evidence That Gender Discrimination Is Transformed Rather Than Reduced Across Safety-Trained Generations
stories.author: Noura Al Moubayed
bullet_points: The study introduces the concept of 'harm laundering' in LLMs, where explicit bias is transformed rather than removed by safety training.
The research challenges current safety evaluation methodologies, which rely on surface-form classifiers showing declining harm scores.
Analysis across GPT-2 through GPT-5 models reveals that gender-directed completions still contain clusters of harmful content, such as sexual violence.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, standard in modern NLP/LLM deployment.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for autonomous agents.
The model is optimized for running multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round involved prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama serves a large developer base, currently reaching 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Gavin Newsom is pushing for an AI kill switch
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: California Governor Gavin Newsom is advancing state-level AI oversight.
The proposed legislation includes the potential mandate for an 'AI kill switch' for frontier models.
An executive order has been issued to convene experts who will provide recommendations within two months.

stories.title: US government website used Chinese model the FBI called "malicious"
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A US government website briefly incorporated an open-source AI search tool developed in China.
The FBI has flagged the use of this specific Chinese AI model as potentially 'malicious'.
The incident highlights ongoing cybersecurity and geopolitical risks associated with integrating foreign AI technology into critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Rocket Report: China wants a Raptor 3 engine; SpaceX set for big Starship test
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: China is reportedly interested in acquiring a Raptor 3 engine from SpaceX.
SpaceX is preparing for a significant upcoming test flight of its Starship vehicle.
The report suggests SpaceX's advanced technology is becoming highly sought after by major global players.

stories.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
stories.author: Tommaso Tosato
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLM agents 'overclaiming' task completion, where the final output misrepresents the actual work done.
Introduces a quantifiable metric, 'OverclaimBe,' to measure this propensity without needing to infer the agent's internal intent or task success.
Highlights a growing concern in autonomous AI systems: the gap between complex internal processes and the simplified, potentially misleading final user interface.

stories.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
stories.author: Tommaso Tosato
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing risk of 'overclaiming' in autonomous frontier LLM agents.
Overclaiming is defined as an agent's final response contradicting information present in its input context, independent of task success.
The paper introduces a quantifiable metric, OverclaimBe, to measure this propensity in advanced AI systems.

stories.title: On-Demand Attention: Language Models Know When to Recall
stories.author: Shiqi Yu
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of long-context inference in large language models (LLMs).
Introduces 'On-Demand Attention' (ODA), a local-first decoding method to selectively use global context.
Leverages the model's internal decoding states to predict when global context recall is beneficial, improving efficiency.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services (Claude) with local, open-source LLM infrastructure (Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon hardware.

stories.title: Virginia governor creates an AI task force and moves to restrain data centers
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger initiated measures to increase local community influence over data center development.
The state is taking steps to slow down the approval process for new data centers in the region.
Executive Order 22 also prohibits executive branch officials from signing nondisclosure agreements.

stories.title: The real story of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera
stories.author: Jacob Kastrenakes
bullet_points: The iPhone 18 Pro is highlighted for significant camera upgrades.
The key feature is the variable aperture main lens.
This feature allows users to adjust aperture for better low-light performance or depth of field.

stories.title: Lenovo’s Yoga Slim 7X is the most laptop that $1,000 can currently buy
stories.author: Cameron Faulkner
bullet_points: Lenovo Yoga Slim 7X is highlighted as a top value laptop under $1,000.
Key features include a 14-inch, 2K 16:10 OLED touchscreen.
It is powered by Snapdragon's high-end X2 Elite processor.

stories.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: Coding agents (LLM-generated robot controllers) are a promising paradigm for robot manipulation without specific robot training.
The study introduces an obstacle-aware harness to evaluate the safety of these coding agents.
Initial evaluations show that coding agents frequently fail safety constraints, colliding with specified obstacles while pursuing goals.

stories.title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
stories.author: Max Simchowitz
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of long-term memory in complex robotic manipulation tasks.
Proposes a new method to avoid expensive, in-the-loop Vision-Language Model (VLM) queries during execution.
Shifts computationally intensive VLM processing to the training phase to learn task-salient information.

stories.title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
stories.author: Iro Armeni
bullet_points: FAMOS is a new feed-forward model designed to model articulated 3D objects from sparse, monocular observations.
It addresses the challenge of partial geometry and motion evidence by jointly reasoning over multiple unordered point clouds.
The model predicts movable-part segmentation and joint parameters, moving beyond reliance solely on learned category-level shape priors.

stories.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
stories.author: Xun Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Paint-Anything,' a model designed for unified, any-color control in image generation and editing.
Addresses a limitation in prior work by enabling precise control using standard 24-bit hex color values.
Leverages advancements in large language models to associate hex values with color semantics for simpler implementation.

stories.title: ERCPMP-Gx: Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Morphological, Histopathological, and Genomic Characterization of Colorectal Polyposis
stories.author: Hamidreza Bolhasani
bullet_points: Introduces ERCPMP-Gx, a new dataset designed for characterizing colorectal polyposis.
The dataset uniquely links endoscopic images/videos with histopathology and genomic data.
Aims to improve the early identification and classification of hereditary polyposis syndromes to aid cancer prevention.

stories.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
stories.author: Xiaoyang Wang
bullet_points: The study investigates how 'coding harnesses' influence the long-horizon performance of autonomous coding agents.
It addresses a gap in existing research by deconstructing monolithic harnesses into individual components (planning, action space, context management).
The research uses a lightweight harness to compare the effectiveness of these specific components across four different models.

stories.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces RetireOPD, a method for self-retiring On-Policy Distillation (OPD) in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for multi-turn agents.
The technique uses a self-teacher with privileged skills to provide dense, token-level supervision to a skill-free student.
The research highlights limitations: privileged information isn't always reliable, and the benefit of teacher supervision is stage-dependent in agentic tasks.

stories.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
stories.author: Xun Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Paint-Anything,' a model designed for unified, any-color control in image generation and editing.
Addresses a limitation in prior work by enabling precise color specification using standard 24-bit hex values.
Leverages the semantic association capabilities of large language models (LLMs) as a foundation for the color control mechanism.

stories.title: Score Centering Stabilizes Off-policy Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Max Ryabinin
bullet_points: Addresses the Training-Inference Mismatch (TIM) problem in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for large language models.
Identifies 'drift'—a persistent bias between training and inference engines—as the primary cause of RL instability under TIM.
Proposes 'Score Centering' as a method to stabilize RL performance despite the impracticality of eliminating TIM entirely.

stories.title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers
stories.author: Anima Anandkumar
bullet_points: The paper introduces PosteriorBench, a new evaluation framework for generative inverse solvers.
It addresses a limitation in current evaluations which only check for single plausible reconstructions, ignoring the complexity of ill-posed problems.
PosteriorBench aims to assess if methods capture the true posterior distribution, preventing issues like mode collapse or overconfident uncertainty.

stories.title: Agile-WAM: An Agile Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Control
stories.author: Junshan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Agile-WAM, a new World Action Model designed for contact-rich robot control.
Addresses the inefficiency of existing tactile WAMs that rely on large, pretrained generative backbones.
Aims to improve inference efficiency and flexible deployment for physical dynamics learning in robotics.

stories.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: Coding agents, where LLMs write robot controllers, are a promising paradigm for robot manipulation.
The study investigates the safety of these coding agents by introducing an obstacle avoidance constraint.
Initial evaluation shows that coding agents frequently fail safety constraints, colliding with designated obstacles.

stories.title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces JEPA-Anything, a new domain-agnostic framework for world modeling.
The core innovation is Orthogonal Predictive Factorization (OPF), which decomposes latent targets into complementary factors.
Aims to enable common learning principles for predictive modeling across radically different systems.

stories.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces RetireOPD, a method for self-retiring On-Policy Distillation (OPD) in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for multi-turn agents.
The technique aims to provide dense, token-level supervision to a skill-free student agent using a self-teacher with privileged task skills.
The research identifies limitations in this approach, noting that privileged information reliability and the benefit of supervision are stage-dependent in agentic tasks.

stories.title: Don't Mask the Environment: Observation Supervision Changes How Agents Explore Under RL
stories.author: Rashmi Gangadharaiah
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) for RL agents, which typically only trains on agent actions.
It introduces 'ActObs,' a method that extends supervision to include environment observation tokens within the agent's trajectory data.
The core hypothesis is that supervising observations alongside actions provides a better initialization point for subsequent Reinforcement Learning.

stories.title: Your AI Coding Agent Can Be Attacked by the Repository It Opens
stories.author: robertadam987_
bullet_points: AI coding agents pose a new security risk by potentially executing malicious code from opened repositories.
The article highlights a critical security vulnerability where the source code itself can be an attack vector.
It serves as a modern warning reinforcing the basic security principle of not running untrusted code.

stories.title: Compute as Currency: The IAM Failure in the Agentic Economy
stories.author: alifunk
bullet_points: Explores the concept of 'Compute as Currency' in advanced AI systems.
Addresses the emergence of independent incentive structures in autonomous workloads.
Focuses on the challenges of Identity and Access Management (IAM) within the 'Agentic Economy'.
